case.summary: Transaction 3447112 for $350.02 on card C11965-K1 was flagged by the bank's second-generation fraud model with an elevated score of 0.994. Investigation revealed that the transaction was executed on device D002318, which is linked to 13 confirmed-fraud closed cases across 13 distinct cards in September 2016. Card C11965-K1 also has three prior confirmed-fraud closed cases from August and September 2016, and the transaction amount represents an anomalous spike with no recurring baseline. Based on the connection to known fraudulent device infrastructure and compromised card history, the transaction is determined to be card-not-present fraud. The card has been blocked and a regulatory report filed.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details unauthorized card-not-present fraud identified on card account C11965-K1 belonging to customer C11965. On November 10, 2016, at 18:59:07 UTC, an unauthorized online transaction (ID 3447112) totaling $350.02 was conducted in billing region 327. The transaction originated from device D002318, which exhibits a device profile of Windows 10 running Chrome 58.0. Graph analysis revealed that device D002318 was directly involved in thirteen confirmed fraudulent closed cases across thirteen different cards during September 2016. Card C11965-K1 has also been subjected to repeated compromises, including three confirmed fraud cases (CC-2220, CC-3391, and CC-3631) in August and September 2016 totaling $1,315.15. The bank's second-generation fraud model scored transaction 3447112 at 0.994, which corresponds to a 92.1% historical fraud rate. Furthermore, the $350.02 transaction represents an elevated single charge compared to the prior fourteen-day range of $99.91 to $250.08, with no recurring payment history. Given the association with known fraudulent hardware infrastructure and compromised account credentials, the transaction is determined to be unauthorized fraud. Card C11965-K1 was blocked to prevent further loss, with the total suspicious exposure in this incident amounting to $350.02.

stop_reason: The investigation concluded under policy section 6 because the fraud probability reached 0.97, well above the 0.85 decisive threshold, supported by multiple independent evidence bases including the calibrated machine-learning model score, device history with 13 confirmed fraud cases, and prior card compromise.
